title: Annotatio VI §.VI open: four objections + biblical for Impious Oral (still pressed)
pass_a_gloss: §. VI. Meanwhile, for admitting Oral Eating of Christ’s Body by the Impious, three arguments in particular — besides those already then overthrown — and one Biblical, laboring under a thoroughly unbiblical consequence, have customarily been brought forward, of which the first they wish to seem drawn from the Nature of the Sacraments; the Second from the Nature of Christ’s given and crucified body; the Third from a Concession once made by the Reformed; to which a Fourth of the Wittenberg Professor is added, sought from the singular use and fruit which the hypothesis of Oral Eating of Christ’s Body by the Impious is to furnish, and from which he also fetches the Necessity and Fundamentality of the Dogma.
pass_b_english: §.VI: for admitting Oral eating of Christ’s body by the Impious, three stock presses remain (plus one biblical) after the earlier ones fell.
From sacrament-nature; from the given/crucified body; from a Reformed concession; and a fourth Wittenberg press from the dogma’s supposed fruit, necessity, and fundamentality.
source_text: §. VI. Interim pro admittenda Impiorum Manducatione Orali Corporis Christi, tria admodum, præter jam tum subversa, & unum Biblicum, consequentia perquam non biblica laborans, adferri in medium consuevêre, quorum primum, à Natura Sacramentorum; Alterum, à Natura dati & crucifixi corporis Christi; Tertium à Concessione Reformatorum semel facta, videri cupiunt desumta; Quibus Quartum Professoris Wittenberg. accedit, petitum ab usu singulari fructuque quem hypothesis de Impiorum Manducatione Corporis Christi Orali, præstet, & à quo etiam Necessitatem Dogmatis ac Fundamentalitatem arcessit.
